_Requirement: Where a keyboard with key repeat is provided, the delay before the key repeat feature is activated must be fixed at, or adjustable to, 2 seconds minimum.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to hardware.
_Guidance: MAS 8.21 - Key Repeat is based on these standards: - Section 508: 407.4 Key Repeat

_Requirement:
Platforms must provide the following assistive technology experiences and provide a discoverable user interface to configure and change them:
•	Enable sequential entry of multiple (chorded) keystrokes; (e.g. Sticky Keys)
•	Provide adjustment of delay before key acceptance (e.g. Filter Keys)
•	Provide adjustment of delay before key acceptance with a delay range that includes 0.5 seconds (e.g. Slow Keys)
•	Provide adjustment of same-key double-strike acceptance with delay adjustable over a range that includes 2 seconds (e.g. Repeat Keys)
•	Allow users to choose visual alternative for audio output (e.g. Notifications in Action Center)
•	Synchronize audio equivalents for visual events (e.g. Notification Sounds and Sound Sentry) 
•	Provide speech output services (e.g. Windows Narrator)
•	Display any captions provided (e.g. Closed Captions)
_Applicability: This rule applies to platforms (e.g., operating systems, browsers, and software that provides ways to run first or third-party apps within the software).
_Guidance: MAS 9.1 - Platform-provided Accessibility User Settings is based on these standards: - Section 508: 502.4 Platform Accessibility Features

_Applicability: This rule applies to platforms (e.g., operating systems, browsers, and software that provides ways to run first or third-party apps within the software).
_Guidance: MAS 9.2 - Platform Accessibility Services is based on these standards: - Section 508: 502.3 Accessibility Services - EN 301 549: 11.5.2.1 Platform accessibility service support for software that provides a user interface (PDF) - EN 301 549: 11.5.2.2 Platform accessibility service support for assistive technologies (PDF)

_Requirement:
Platforms must provide sufficient modes of operation for user control over platform accessibility features documented as intended for users. Platforms must provide accessibility features for the following user personas: 
1.	No Vision
2.	Limited Vision 
3.	Without the Perception of Color
4.	With Photosensitive Seizure Triggers
5.	No Hearing
6.	Limited Hearing
7.	Limited Manipulation (e.g. tremors)
8.	Limited Strength (e.g. arthritis and cerebral palsy)
9.	Limited Reach (e.g. quadriplegia) 
10.	No Reach (e.g. ALS)
11.	Limited Vocal Capability
12.	Limited Cognition
13.	Combination of Limited Vision and Limited Hearing
_Applicability: This rule applies to platforms (e.g., operating systems, browsers, and software that provides ways to run first or third-party apps within the software).
_Guidance: MAS 9.3 - Platform Assistive Technologies is based on these standards: - Section 508: 502.2.1 User Control of Accessibility Features - EN 301 549: 11.6.1 User control of accessibility features (PDF)

_Title: Documentation of Accessibility and Compatibility Features
_Requirement:
All features and functionality designed for people with disabilities must be explained in accessible documentation.
Documentation should be localized into relevant local languages consistent with Microsoft's general practices related to help documentation
_Applicability: This requirement applies to documentation (for example, help files, instructions, user manuals, and web pages) for all products and services.
_Guidance: MAS 10.1 - Accessibility and Compatibility Features is based on these standards: - Section 508: 602.2 Accessibility and Compatibility Features - EN 301 549: 12.1.1 Accessibility and compatibility features (PDF)

_Requirement:
Documentation (including help documentation) must be provided in an accessible electronic format.

Documentation also must be provided to customers upon request in alternate formats (for example, Braille, audio) at no additional cost. Microsoft provides alternate formats of documentation to customers upon request through the [Disability Answer Desk](https://www.microsoft.com/en-US/Accessibility/disability-answer-desk).
_Applicability: This requirement applies to documentation (for example, help files, instructions, user manuals, and web pages) for all products and services.
_Guidance: MAS 10.2 - Product Documentation Format is based on these standards: - Section 508: 602.3 Electronic Support Documentation - Section 508: 602.4 Alternate Formats for Non-Electronic Support Documentation - EN 301 549: 12.1.2 Accessible documentation (PDF)

_Requirement: Support services should be well-versed in accessibility, along with offering documentation in accessible formats. Microsoft meets this requirement by offering support to customers with disabilities through the [Disability Answer Desk](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/answerdesk/accessibility).
_Applicability:
This requirement applies to support services: 

- help (for example, call centers, technical support, and training services) and 
- documentation (for example, help files, user manuals, instructions, web pages).
_Guidance:
MAS 10.3 - Support Services is based on these standards: - Section 508: - 603.2 Information on Accessibility and Compatibility Features - 603.3 Accommodation of Communication Needs

- EN 301 549 V3.2.1 (PDF) - 12.2.1 General (informative) - 12.2.2 Information on accessibility and compatibility features - 12.2.3 Effective communication - 12.2.4 Accessible documentation

_Requirement: The means to activate accessibility features must be accessible.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to websites, electronic documents, and any software that has a user interface.
_Guidance: MAS 11.1 - Activation of Accessibility Features is based on these standards: - EN 301 549: 5.2 Activation of Accessibility Features (PDF)

_Requirement: Products or services that use a biometric form of user identification must provide an alternative method for identification that is either non-biometric (for example, entering a password) or a second biometric form using dissimilar biological characteristics (for example, using a retinal scan instead of a fingerprint).
_Applicability: This requirement applies to anything that requires a biometric form of identification, (for example, fingerprints or iris patterns).
_Guidance: MAS 11.2 - Biometric ID is based on these standards: - Section 508: 403.1 General - EN 301 549: 5.3 Biometrics (PDF)

_Requirement: Where key repeat is provided and the key repeat cannot be turned off: a) the delay before the key repeat must be adjustable to at least 2 seconds; and b) the key repeat rate must be adjustable down to one character per 2 seconds.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to software with a user interface and platforms.
_Guidance: MAS 11.3.1 - Key Repeat is based on these standards: - EN 301 549: 5.7 Key repeat (PDF)

_Requirement: Where a keyboard or keypad is provided, the delay after any keystroke, during which an additional key-press will not be accepted if it is identical to the previous keystroke, must be adjustable up to at least 0.5 seconds.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to software with a user interface and platforms.
_Guidance: MAS 11.3.2 - Double Strike Key Acceptance is based on these standards: - EN 301 549: 5.8 Double-strike key acceptance (PDF)

_Requirement:
No feature should require more than one control to be activated simultaneously to operate it. There must be at least one mode of operation and information retrieval that does not require simultaneous user actions. However, sequential operation of two controls to engage a feature is acceptable via menu or special operating mode the user can select and de-select.  

Having to use both hands to open the lid of a laptop, having to press two or more keys at the same time or having to touch a surface with more than one finger are examples of simultaneous user actions.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to software with a user interface and hardware.
_Guidance: MAS 11.3.3 - Simultaneous User Actions is based on these standards: - EN 301 549: 5.9 Simultaneous user actions (PDF)

_Requirement: All accessibility information must be preserved when transmitting, receiving, converting or processing data, file formats, or content.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to anything that transmits, receives, or processes data, file formats, or content.
_Guidance: MAS 11.4 - Preserving Accessibility Information is based on these standards: - Section 508: 404.1 Preservation of Information Provided for Accessibility - EN 301 549: 5.4 Preservation of accessibility information during conversion (PDF)

_Requirement:
Voice over IP (VoIP, both interconnected and non-interconnected) services used for in-game chat must implement the Xbox and Windows platform speech-to-text/text-to-speech feature to make the audio chat accessible to people who cannot hear, have hearing loss, cannot speak, or have speech impairments.  

The feature is “accessible” if the input, control, and mechanical functions are locatable, identifiable, and operable for a person with a disability.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to interconnected or non-interconnected VoIP services used for in-game chat
_Guidance: MAS 11.5 - Speech-to-Text and Text-to-Speech for In-game Chat is based on these standards: - FCC: 47 CFR §14.20 – Obligations for Covered Communications Services - FCC: 47 CFR §14.21 – Performance Objectives

_Requirement: has Anything that has a locking or toggle control that is visually presented to the user must have at least one mode of operation where the status of all locking or toggle controls can be determined through touch or sound without operating the control.
_Applicability: This requirement applies anything that have a locking or toggle control that is visually presented to the user.
_Guidance: MAS 11.7 - Tactile or Auditory Status is based on these standards: - EN 301 549: 5.6.1 Tactile or auditory status (PDF)

_Requirement: Anything that has a locking or toggle control that is non-visually presented to the user (such as through sound or touch), must have at least one mode of operation where the status of all locking or toggle controls can be visually determined when the control is presented.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to anything that has a locking or toggle control that is non-visually presented to the user.
_Guidance: MAS 11.8 - Visual Status is based on these standards: - EN 301 549: 5.6.2 Visual status (PDF)

_Requirement:
For devices that are closed or have closed functionality, the closed functionality must be operable without requiring the user to attach, connect, or install assistive technology (not including personal headsets or induction loops).  

Closed Functionality standards require that alternative access features be built into a product so users do not have to attach an assistive device to it. Additional requirements address mechanisms for private listening (handset or a standard headphone jack), touchscreens, auditory output and adjustable volume controls, and location of controls in accessible reach ranges.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to devices that are self-contained, closed products.. Examples include copiers, printers, fax machines, calculators, and information kiosks.

_Requirement:
Platforms must provide UI that enable users to discover and change the
following accessibility settings:

-   High contrast

-   Foreground and background color as applied to the text and
    background of content

-   An alternative to audio alerts such as a visual alert (e.g., Windows
    Sound Sentry) or a tactile alert (e.g., vibrating phone)

-   System-level volume for platforms that enable audio presentation

-   Customized key input

    -   Modifier key lock such as Windows Sticky Keys

    -   Key input filter such as Windows Filter Keys

    -   Audio key lock such as Windows Toggle Keys

-   Customized text size up to 200%

-   Customized font type (must include one serif and one sans serif
    type)

-   Customized visual indication of user input focus

    -   Focus rectangle thickness

    -   Caret blink rate

    -   Caret width

    -   Mouse pointer size and color

-   Visual indication of keyboard shortcuts such as underline access
    keys

-   Alternative to mouse movement such as Windows Mouse Keys.
_Applicability:
This rule applies if your product allows the running of applications by
providing an underlying software or hardware layer that serves as the
operating environment, architecture, or accessibility API(s).

_Requirement:
Avoid forced focus changes that are not initiated by the user. Ensure
all focus changes that occur are a result of user action and that the
user expects the change.
_Applicability:
Focus is used to indicate the specific UI element is ready to receive
input via a device or speech. As the user navigates and interacts with
the UI, focus changes from one element to another. UI elements that can
receive focus and are covered under this rule are interactive elements,
meaning they respond to user input. Examples include text, menus,
buttons, links, and list boxes.

For the purposes of MAS 06 - On Focus, input devices are defined as, but
not limited to:

-   Physical keyboards

-   On-screen keyboards

-   Xbox controllers

-   Media Center controllers (remote controls)

-   Keypads or buttons on handheld devices (both on-screen and hardware)

This applies to all configurations if a configuration is allowed that
includes attaching a keyboard or keypad with physical buttons. The
application and platform must be responsive to programmatic synthesis of
keyboard input even when a keyboard is not attached. This is critical to
techniques used by some assistive technology applications such as screen
readers and voice recognition software.

If your product or service does not support focus, or is in a mode where
focus behavior is not being used, then this rule does not apply. The
primary example is a touchscreen. All UI elements on a touchscreen
responding to touch or gestures are ready for input. No one element
currently "has focus."

_Requirement:
Ensure that users can move focus out of a control by using a method
consistent with the method used to move focus into the control. [Ensure
keyboard focus is not
trapped](https://www.webaccessibility.com/best_practices.php?best_practice_id=1243).
_Applicability:
Does your product, service, tool or content support focus and allow user
input or interaction?

-   If yes, this rule applies.

-   If no, this rule does not apply.

Focus is used to indicate the UI element that can receive input. UI
elements that can receive focus and are covered under this rule are
interactive elements, meaning they respond to user input. Examples
include text, menus, buttons, links, and list boxes. Input devices
include but are not limited to:

-   Physical keyboards

-   On-screen keyboards

-   Xbox controllers

-   Media Center controllers (TV remote controls)

-   Keypads or buttons on handheld devices (both on-screen and hardware)

-   Voice control

You have met this rule if users can navigate to and from all UI elements
that should receive focus using a consistent navigation method.

against the background, except:

    requirement.

_Requirement:
Where ICT provides real-time voice-based communication and also provides
voice mail, auto-attendant, or interactive voice response facilities,
the ICT should offer users a means to access the information and carry
out the tasks provided by the ICT without the use of hearing or speech.

Additionally, voicemail, interactive voice response (IVR) systems, and
related telecommunication functions that provide playback must include
player controls that allow users to pause, skip, rewind, and repeat all
messages and prompts.
_Applicability:
This rule applies if your product has either of the following:

-   Includes or enables voice communications or other audio information
    over the public-switched telephone network (PSTN) or via Voice over
    IP (VOIP); and

-   Includes related functionality such as VoIP, voice mail, interactive
    voice response systems, caller ID, call waiting, call forwarding,
    speed dialing, repeat dialing, or computer provide directory
    assistance.

_Requirement:
Caller identification and telecommunication functions that are visually
displayed must provide non-visual alternatives to both users who are
blind and those with restricted vision.
_Applicability:
This rule applies if your product has either of the following:

-   Includes or enables voice communications or other audio information
    over the public-switched telephone network (PSTN) or by using a
    broadband Internet connection to and from the PSTN.

-   Includes related functionality such as VoIP, voice mail, interactive
    voice response systems, caller ID, call waiting, call forwarding,
    speed dialing, repeat dialing, or computer provide directory
    assistance.

_Requirement:
On telecommunication products that have adjustable volume, there must be
an automatic volume reset function that sets the volume back to the
default level.
_Applicability:
This rule applies if your telecommunications product:

> has a handset, headset, earphone, or other transducer near the ear.
> Assume that the default volume level is safe, clear, and audible for
> fully able users. Note that personal communications devices such as
> cell phones do not typically default.

_Requirement:
Platforms must provide and document platform accessibility services for
interoperability with assistive technologies (ATs). For example, Windows
provides UI Automation (UIA).
_Applicability:

-   Allows the running of applications, by providing an underlying
    software or hardware layer, which serves as the operating
    environment, architecture or accessibility API(s). This includes,
    for example, Windows, Xbox, Windows Phone, but not Office, Microsoft
    Edge, or Azure.

-   Allows second- or third-party applications to run on your platform.

shall be programmatically determinable. Where the platform provides

the accessibility API.

accessibility API. See [Platform Support Guidelines for MAS
33A-M](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/msenable/_layouts/15/WopiFrame.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B0AEC6C62-B816-4F34-B212-DBF763816353%7D&file=PlatformSupportMAS33AthruM.docx&action=default).

platform limitation, the MAS is considered "supported" but the platform
limitations should be noted in the "remarks and explanation" field of
any conformance statement.

_Title: Tracking of Focus and Selection Attributes
_Requirement:

focus, text insertion point, and selection attributes (e.g. whether text

point, and selection attributes of user interface components must be
provided to the accessibility APIs.

accessibility API. See [Platform Support Guidelines for MAS
33A-M](https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/msenable/_layouts/15/WopiFrame.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B0AEC6C62-B816-4F34-B212-DBF763816353%7D&file=PlatformSupportMAS33AthruM.docx&action=default).

limitations should be noted in the "remarks and explanation" field of
any conformance statement.

configured as part of the platform must ensure the availability of
assistive technologies for users with disabilities (including
individuals without vision, with limited vision, without speech, or with
limited manipulation, reach, or strength).
_Applicability:
This rule applies if your product has either of the following:

-   Allows the running of applications, by providing an underlying
    software or hardware layer, which serves as the operating
    environment, architecture or accessibility API(s). This includes,
    for example, Windows, Xbox, Windows Phone, but not Office, Microsoft
    Edge, or Azure.

-   Allows second- or third-party applications to run on your platform.

_Requirement:
For any product, service, tool, or content, all user tasks (for example,
text input, interaction with controls, and navigation) must be operable
through the UI by using only physical or on-screen keyboard interfaces
(on platforms that support keyboard interfaces). This includes a
requirement to support both onscreen and physical keyboards for mobile
apps.

Disabled controls may be in the tab order and they need to clearly
indicate that they are disabled.
_Applicability:
Does your product, service, tool or content run on a platform that
supports keyboard interfaces (such as physical or on-screen keyboard)
and allows user input or interaction?

-   If yes, this rule applies.

-   If no, this rule does not apply.

_Requirement:

must provide an alternative method for identification that is either
non-biometric (e.g., entering a password) or a second biometric form
using dissimilar biological characteristics (e.g., using a retinal scan
instead of a fingerprint).

identification (such as fingerprints or iris patterns)?

-   If yes, this rule applies.

-   If no, this rule does not apply.

_Requirement:
Where software/application provides a user interface it shall interoperate with those documented [accessibility features](#accessibility-features-found-in-the-ease-of-access-settings-for-windows-10) that are defined in platform documentation. This includes ensuring that the following can be programmatically determined by the Platform assistive technology (usually via the use of Platform APIs): - role, state(s), boundary, name, and description; - row and column of each cell in a data table, including headers of the row and column if present; - the current value of a user interface element and any minimum or maximum values of the range; - relationship that a user interface element has as a label for another element, or of being labelled by another element; - relationship between a user interface element and any parent or children elements; - text contents, text attributes, and the boundary of text; - available actions that can be executed on a user interface element (and allow the programmatic execution of the actions); - information and mechanisms necessary to track focus, text insertion point, and selection attributes of user interface elements; - changes in those programmatically determinable attributes of user interface elements; Allow platform assistive technology to: - execute available actions on a user interface element; - modify track focus, text insertion point, and selection attributes of user interface elements; - programmatically modify states and properties of user interface elements; - modify values and text of user interface elements using the input methods of the platform; This also includes ensuring that [images and icons do not disappear when high contrast mode is enabled](http://blogs.msdn.com/b/wsdevsol/archive/2014/02/20/accessibility-gotchas-2-high-contrast.aspx). "Accessibility features" are defined as those found in the new "modern" Ease of Access Settings (Settings \> Ease of Access), not the old Ease of Access Center. This provides us with a consistent definition between PC and Mobile for where the features are found. ### Accessibility Features found in the Ease of Access Settings for Windows 10 Settings \> Ease of Access (NOT the old Ease of Access Center found on the PC)
Accessibility Features for Win10 PC and Mobile
PC Mobile

Mouse Pointer Size
Mouse Pointer Color
Mouse Keys
Play Animations
Show Notifications (length of time setting)
Cursor Thickness
Visual Notification of Sound (Sound Sentry)
Visual Feedback when Touching the Screen

stream to enable the transmission of audio emergency information.

devices with preinstalled video players and devices that can record
video programming must meet closed caption requirements, and, depending
upon the content the player supports, video description and emergency
information secondary audio stream requirements.

_Title: Hearing Aid Compatibility (HAC) for Mobile Handsets (T mode)
_Requirement:
Mobile handsets must provide a means of magnetic coupling with hearing
technologies (e.g., hearing aids, cochlear implants and assistive
listening devices) with an FCC rating of T3 or T4. "T" refers to the
phone"s coupling ability and is intended for use with hearing aids in
the telecoil mode. The "T" rating of HAC-compliant devices must be
included on product packages or in product literature.
_Applicability:
This rule applies if the mobile handset is manufactured or imported for
use in the United States (including US territories) and is used with
voice communication services over a mobile operator"s cellular network.
A phablet is considered a mobile handset for this purpose. A tablet or
PC that is not typically held to the ear is not considered a mobile
handset covered by this rule.

_Title: Hearing Aid Compatibility (HAC) for Mobile Handsets (M mode)
_Requirement:
Mobile handsets must reduce interference with hearing technologies
(e.g., hearing aids, cochlear implants and assistive listening devices)
to the lowest possible level that will allow use of the product. To be
compliant with Hearing Aid Compatibility (HAC), the phone must have an
FCC rating of M3 or M4. "M" refers to the microphone mode. The "M"
rating of HAC-compliant devices must be included on product packages or
in product literature.
_Applicability:
This rule applies if the mobile handset is manufactured or imported for
use in the United States (including US territories) and is used with
voice communication services over a mobile operator"s cellular network.
A phablet is considered a mobile handset for this purpose. A tablet or
PC that is not typically held to the ear is not considered a mobile
handset covered by this rule.

_Title: User Interfaces, Video Programming Guides and Menus
_Requirement:
Any User Interface (UI) that a person must navigate in order to launch
applications that play video programming must be accompanied by audio
output (such as through a screen reader). The following functions, if
offered through an onscreen text menu, must be accompanied by audible
output:

1.  *Power on / off*

2.  *Volume adjust / mute *

3.  *Channel / program selection (including on-demand programming)*
    Function that allows the user to select channels and programs (e.g.,
    via physical numeric or channel up/channel down buttons or via on
    screen guides and menus)

4.  *Display channel / program information (including on-demand
    programming)*

5.  *Configuration / set-up (for example, language selection, parental
    controls)*  
    Function that allows the user to access and change configuration or
    setup options (e.g., configuration of video display and audio
    settings, selection of preferred language for onscreen guides or
    menus, etc.).

6.  *Enable / disable closed captioning *

7.  *Configuration of closed captioning options (for example, changing
    font size, color) *

8.  *Enable / disable video description *

9.  *Display configuration info  
    *Function that allows the user to display how user preferences are
    currently configured

10. *Playback functions (for example, play, pause, rewind, fast forward,
    stop, and record) *

11. *Input selection* Function that allows the user to select their
    preferred input source.

Covered devices and applications are not required to include any or all
of these functions, but if they are included, they must be accessible.

If any of these 11 functions are offered other than through on-screen
menus"for example, power-on functionality could be activated via the
hardware"then those functions must still be accessible for individuals
without vision, with low vision and limited or no hearing, and with
limited or no color perception.

A feature is "accessible" if the input, control, and mechanical
functions are locatable, identifiable, and operable for a person with a
disability. A person with a disability should have at least one method
for using the feature that provides equivalent functionality as is
available to users without a disability. For example, the power-on
mechanical control should be tactilely discernable to aid use by
individuals with visual impairments; patterns should be used to augment
color cues for those with limited color perception.

Video programming is programming by, or comparable to, programming
provided by a television broadcast station, including when such video
programming is delivered using Internet Protocol (IP). It does not
include user-generated content, unless that content is subsequently
broadcast on television with captions.
_Applicability:
> This rule applies to:

-   Devices that receive or playback video programming (such as the Xbox
    One, Xbox 360, Xbox Blu-ray/DVD player, PCs, Phones and Tablets,
    Surface, and SurfaceHub),

-   Devices that have preinstalled video applications, whether our own
    or third party (such as the Xbox OneGuide, Microsoft Movies & TV,
    Groove, Windows Media Player, and preinstalled third-party
    applications such as Netflix, Hulu, or Amazon), and

-   Video applications that we direct people to use to access video
    programming,

> If those devices have

-   Onscreen menus that offer any of 11 specific video playback
    functions, or

-   Offer video playback functionality in a manner other than onscreen
    text menus, such as a power on/off on hardware.

_Title: Closed Captioning, Video Description and Emergency Information Activation
_Requirement:
If your product or service offers closed captioning or video description
functionality, that function must be activated by an easy-to-locate and
simple-to-use mechanism such as a button, key, or icon.

Players that are preinstalled or that Microsoft directs consumers to use
in order to access linear programming on our devices (such as Xbox TV)
and players that record video programming comparable to that provided by
broadcasters must provide a simple and easy to use mechanism (such as a
button, key, or icon) for activating the secondary audio stream for
audible emergency information.

Video programming is programming provided by, or generally considered
comparable to programming provided by, a television broadcast station
(whether distributed over the air, by cable or satellite), but not
including consumer-generated media.

Linear programming is prescheduled (as opposed to on-demand) broadcast
programming delivered via cable, satellite, or over the air.
_Applicability:
This rule applies to:

-   Devices that receive, play back, or record video programming (such
    as but not limited to the Xbox One, Xbox 360, Xbox Blu-ray/DVD
    player, PCs, Phones and Tablets, and Surface);

-   Devices that have preinstalled video applications, our own or third
    party (such as the Xbox OneGuide, Microsoft Movies & TV, Groove,
    Windows Media Player, or preinstalled third-party applications such
    as Netflix, Hulu, or Amazon); and

-   Players that are preinstalled or that Microsoft directs consumers to
    use in order to access linear programming on our devices (such as
    Xbox TV).

_Title: Visual indicator of audio with RTT
_Requirement:
Anything that provide two-way voice communication and real-time text (RTT) must provide a real-time visual indicator of audio activity. 

Note: The visual indicator may be a simple character position on the display that flickers on and off to reflect audio activity, or presentation of the information in another way that can be both visible to sighted users and passed on to deaf-blind users who are using a braille display.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to anything that provides two-way voice communication and real-time text (RTT).
_Guidance: MAS 6.2.2.4 - Visual indicator of audio with RTT is based on these standards: - EN 301 549: 6.2.2.4 Visual indicator of audio with RTT (PDF)

_Requirement:
Devices and video players capable of displaying audiovisual content with closed captions must provide a way for users to change caption display characteristics, except where the captions are displayed as unmodifiable characters. 

Notes:
- Defining the background and foreground color of captions, font type, size, opacity of the background box of captions, and the contour or border of the fonts can contribute to meeting this requirement. 
- Captions that are bitmap images are examples of unmodifiable characters.
_Applicability:
This requirement applies to devices and video players capable of displaying audiovisual content with closed captions

Note: See [MAS 7.1.4.1](https://aka.ms/mas7.1.4.1) for devices and video players subject to the CVAA. These include video players (for example, apps and browsers with built-in players), devices with preinstalled video players, and devices that can record or play back video.

This requirement does not apply to: 
- applications with built-in players that are only used for video creation or editing 
- video communications (See the MAS 6.6 series for applicable requirements.)
_Guidance: MAS 7.1.4 - Caption characteristics is based on these standards: - EN 301 549: 7.1.4 Captions characteristics (PDF)

_Requirement: **As of August 17, 2026:** Devices capable of displaying video programming must provide APIs (or a similar method such as an SDK) that make device [caption characteristics settings](https://aka.ms/mas7.1.4) available to applications that play back video programming.

This requirement applies to devices capable of playing video programming such as laptops and gaming consoles. 

The FCC defines “video programming” as “programming provided by, or generally considered comparable to programming provided by, a television broadcast station, but not including consumer-generated media.” 

This requirement does not apply to video communications (See the MAS 6.6 series for applicable requirements.)

_Requirement:

- for audible information, without the use of hearing
- for spoken commands, without the use of speech
- for visual information, without the use of vision.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to anything that provides real-time video communications and voicemail, auto-attendant, or interactive voice response (IVR).
_Guidance: MAS 6.7 - Alternatives to Video-based Services is based on these standards: - EN 301 549: 6.6 Alternatives to video-based services (PDF).

_Requirement:
Anything that can be used by two or more people to communicate in real time using video must support the following performance requirements: 

**Resolution:**

- Must support at least Quarter Video Graphics Array (QVGA, 320 x 240) resolution 
- Should preferably support at least VGA (640 x 480) resolution 

**Frame rate:**

- Must support a frame rate of at least 20 frames per second (FPS) 
- Should preferably support a frame rate of at least 30 frames per second (FPS) with or without sign language in the video stream
_Applicability: This requirement applies to anything that provides real-time video communications.

_Title: Hearing Aid Compatibility (HAC) for Mobile Handsets - Product Documentation
_Requirement:
The hearing aid compatibility of of mobile handsets must be documented on product packages, in product inserts and user manuals, and on websites.
If you are designing a mobile handset, please reach out immediately to the Accessibility Technical Team [accTT@microsoft.com](accTT@microsoft.com "accTT@microsoft.com") for detailed requirements.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to mobile handsets manufactured or imported for use in the United States (including US territories) and used with a mobile operator’s voice communication service. A tablet or PC that is not typically held to the ear is not considered a mobile handset covered by this requirement.
_Guidance:

_Requirement:
Authoring tools must prompt users to create or edit applications, services, tools, and content that is accessible. 

Notes: 

A prompt is any authoring tool-initiated request for a decision or piece of information from authors. The term covers both requests that must be responded to immediately (for example, modal dialog boxes) as well as less urgent requests (for example, underlining a misspelled word). Authoring tools containing accessibility checkers satisfy this requirement, as does providing the ability for users to add alt-text to images.
_Applicability:
This requirement applies to authoring tools. An authoring tool is any software that can be used by authors, alone or collaboratively, to create or modify content or to develop applications or services, for use by other people (other authors or end users). 

Notes:
- “Content” includes documents, websites, blogs, images, video, and user-generated content. 
- Any software that offers an ability for authors or end users to create rich text content is considered an authoring tool. 
- Any software that **only** offers an ability for authors or end users to create plain text content is **not** considered an authoring tool.
_Guidance: MAS 5.3.1 - Prompts is based on these standards: - Section 508: 504.3 Prompts.

**Annex I, Section I**
General accessibility requirements related to all products covered by this Directive in accordance with Article 2(1):

Products must be designed and produced in such a way as to maximise their foreseeable use by persons with disabilities and shall be accompanied where possible in or on the product by accessible information on their functioning and on their accessibility features.
1. Requirements on the provision of information:
b) the instructions for use of a product, where not provided on the product itself but made available through the use of the product or through other means such as a website, including the accessibility functions of the product, how to activate them and their interoperability with assistive solutions shall be publicly available when the product is placed on the market and shall:
(i) be made available via more than one sensory channel;
(ii) be presented in an understandable way;
(iii) be presented to users in ways they can perceive;
(iv) be presented in fonts of adequate size and suitable shape, taking into account foreseeable conditions of use and using sufficient contrast, as well as adjustable spacing between letters, lines and paragraphs;
(v) with regard to content, be made available in text formats that can be used for generating alternative assistive formats to be presented in different ways and via more than one sensory channel;
(vi) be accompanied by an alternative presentation of any non-textual content;
(vii) include a description of the user interface of the product (handling, control and feedback, input and output) which is provided in accordance with point 2; the description shall indicate for each of the points in point 2 whether the product provides those features;
(viii) include a description of the functionality of the product which is provided by functions aiming to address the needs of persons with disabilities in accordance with point 2; the description shall indicate for each of the points in point 2 whether the product provides those features;
(ix) include a description of the software and hardware interfacing of the product with assistive devices; the description shall include a list of those assistive devices which have been tested together with the product.

2. User interface and functionality design:
The product, including its user interface, shall contain features, elements and functions, that allow persons with disabilities to access, perceive, operate, understand and control the product by ensuring that: (a) when the product provides for communication, including interpersonal communication, operation, information, control and orientation, it shall do so via more than one sensory channel; this shall include providing alternatives to vision, auditory, speech and tactile elements;

c) when the product uses visual elements it shall provide for flexible magnification, brightness and contrast for communication, information and operation, as well as ensure interoperability with programmes and assistive devices to navigate the interface;
(d) when the product uses colour to convey information, indicate an action, require a response or identify elements, it shall provide an alternative to colour;
(e) when the product uses audible signals to convey information, indicate an action, require a response or identify elements, it shall provide an alternative to audible signals;
(f) when the product uses visual elements it shall provide for flexible ways of improving vision clarity;
(g) when the product uses audio it shall provide for user control of volume and speed, and enhanced audio features including the reduction of interfering audio signals from surrounding products and audio clarity;
(h) when the product requires manual operation and control, it shall provide for sequential control and alternatives to fine motor control, avoiding the need for simultaneous controls for manipulation, and shall use tactile discernible parts;
(i) the product shall avoid modes of operation requiring extensive reach and great strength;
(j) the product shall avoid triggering photosensitive seizures;
(k) the product shall protect the user�s privacy when he or she uses the accessibility features;
(l) the product shall provide an alternative to biometrics identification and control;
(m) the product shall ensure the consistency of the functionality and shall provide enough, and flexible amounts of, time for interaction;
(n) the product shall provide software and hardware for interfacing with the assistive technologies.

_Requirement:
When a [user interface component](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#dfn-user-interface-components) receives keyboard focus, the component is not entirely hidden due to author-created content.

Note: Where content in a configurable interface can be repositioned by the user, then only the initial positions of user-movable content are considered for testing and meeting this requirement. 

Note: Content opened by the user may obscure the component receiving focus. If the user can reveal the focused component without advancing the keyboard focus, the component with focus is not considered hidden due to author-created content.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to websites, electronic documents, and any software that has a user interface.
_Guidance: MAS 2.4.11 – Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) is based on this standard: - WCAG 2.2: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)

_Requirement: All functionality that uses a [dragging movement](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html#dfn-dragging-movement) for operation can be achieved by a [single pointer](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html#dfn-single-pointer) without dragging, unless dragging is [essential](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html#dfn-essential) or the functionality is determined by the [user agent](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html#dfn-user-agent) and not modified by the author.
_Applicability:
This requirement applies to websites, electronic documents, and software that  interprets pointer actions. 

This requirement does not apply to actions that are required to operate the user agent, underlying platform software, or assistive technology
_Guidance: MAS 2.5.7 – Dragging Movements is based on this standard: - WCAG 2.2: Dragging Movements

_Applicability: This requirement applies to websites, electronic documents, and any software that has a user interface.
_Guidance: MAS 2.5.8 – Target Size (Minimum) is based on this standard: - WCAG 2.2: Target Size (Minimum)

_Requirement:
If a [Web page](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-help#dfn-web-page) contains any of the following help [mechanisms](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-help#): - Human contact details - Human contact mechanism - Self-help option - A fully automated contact mechanism and those mechanisms are repeated • On multiple Web pages within a [set of Web pages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-help#dfn-set-of-web-pages), • In multiple electronic documents within a [set of electronic documents](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#set-of-documents), or • In software within a [set of software programs](https://w3c.github.io/wcag2ict/#set-of-software-programs), the help mechanisms occur in the same order relative to other content, unless a change is initiated by the user.
Note: Help mechanisms may be provided directly on the web page, in the electronic document or software, or may be provided via a direct link to a different web page, electronic document, or software containing the information. Note: For this requirement, "the same order relative to other content" can be thought of as how the content is ordered when the web page, electronic document, or software is serialized. The visual position of a help mechanism is likely to be consistent across web pages, electronic documents, or software for the same content variation (for example, CSS break-point). The user can initiate a change, such as changing the web page's, electronic document’s, or software’s zoom or orientation, which may trigger a different content layout variation. This requirement is concerned with relative order across web pages, electronic documents, or software displayed in the same content layout variation (for example, same zoom level and orientation).
_Applicability: This requirement applies to websites, electronic documents, and any software that has a user interface.
_Guidance: MAS 3.2.6 – Consistent Help is based on this standard: - WCAG 2.2: Consistent Help

_Requirement:
Information previously entered by or provided to the user that is required to be entered again in the same [process](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/redundant-entry.html#dfn-process) is either: - Auto-populated, or - Available for the user to select.
Except when: - Re-entering the information is [essential](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/redundant-entry.html#dfn-essential), - The information is required to ensure the security of the content, or - Previously entered information is no longer valid.

_Requirement:

**Alternative:**

Another authentication method that does not rely on a cognitive function test. 

**Mechanism:**

A [mechanism](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/accessible-authentication-minimum#dfn-mechanism) is available to assist the user in completing the cognitive function test. 

**Object Recognition:**

The cognitive function test is to recognize objects. 

**Personal Content:**

The cognitive function test is to identify [non-text content](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/accessible-authentication-minimum#dfn-non-text-content) the user provided to the Web site, electronic document, or software.

_Requirement:
Anything that can be used by two or more people to communicate in real time using video and provides speaker identification for voice users must provide a means for speaker identification for real-time signing and sign language users once the start of signing has been indicated.
**Note:** the speaker ID can be in the same location as for voice users for multiparty calls **Note:** this mechanism might be triggered manually by a user, or automatically where this is technically achievable
_Applicability: This requriement applies to anything that provides real-time video communications.
_Guidance: MAS 6.6.3 - Speaker Identification with Video (Sign Language) Communication is based on these standards: - EN 301 549: • EN 301 549 V.3.2.1 (PDF): - 6.5.1 General (informative) - 6.5.6 Speaker Identification with Video (Sign Language) Communication

_Requirement:
**As of January 12, 2027**: Anything that can be used by two or more people to communicate in real time using video must support the use of sign language interpretation by: 

Enabling the use of sign language interpretation provided by third parties, including enabling users to send requests for sign language interpreters to video relay services and other providers. 

Providing user interface controls that enable users to activate and adjust the display of speakers and signers, including:
•	the ability to minimize, expand, relocate, and hide windows
•	enabling users to edit their display name before or after joining a call.
_Applicability: This rule applies to products and services that provide real-time video communications.
_Guidance:

_Requirement:
**As of January 12, 2027**: Anything that can be used by two or more people to communicate in real time using video must: Provide first-party captions that accurately and synchronously display the spoken communications. • Accurately means that captioning matches the spoken words of a conversation, in the order spoken, verbatim, without summarizing or paraphrasing, sufficiently to enable a user to understand what is being said. - **Note:** “Verbatim” does not mean 100% accuracy. • Synchronously means that, to the greatest extent possible, the captions begin to appear at the time that the corresponding speech or sounds begin and end approximately when the speech or sounds end, are delivered fast enough to keep up with the speed of those words and sounds, and remain displayed long enough to be read by the user.

Enable users to connect with third-party captioning services so that captions provided by such services appear on the user’s video conference screen. • Note: Connection to third-party captioning services may be achieved by providing an API. • Note: Microsoft is not responsible for ensuring that third-party captions are accurate and synchronous. However, Microsoft products and services must not impair or impede the delivery of third-party captions.

Provide user interface controls that enable users to activate and adjust the display of captions, including: • changing the size, font, and on-screen location of captions • adjusting the color and opacity of both the captions and the caption background.
_Applicability: This requirement applies to products and services that provide real-time video communications.
_Guidance:

	- [47 CFR §14.21(b)(4) Interoperable Video Conferencing Service](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/part-14/section-14.21#p-14.21(b)(4))

_Title: User Controls for Caption Characteristics (CVAA Devices and Players)
_Requirement:
Devices capable of playing video programming and video players that Microsoft either preinstalls on those devices or requires end users to install on those devices must support the specific technical features for closed captions described below: **Presentation:** Captioning shall be implemented such that the caption text may be displayed within one or separate caption windows and supporting the following modes: - a. text that appears a- ll at once (pop-on) - b. text that scrolls up as new text appears (roll-up) and, - c. text where each new letter or word is displayed as it arrives (paint-on). **Character color:** Captioning shall be implemented such that characters may be displayed in the 64 colors defined in CEA-708 and such that users are provided with the ability to override the authored color for characters and select from a palette of at least 8 colors including: white, black, red, green, blue, yellow, magenta, and cyan. **Character opacity:** Captioning shall be implemented such that users are provided with the ability to vary the opacity of captioned text and select between opaque and semi-transparent opacities. **Character size:** Captioning shall be implemented such that users are provided with the ability to vary the size of captioned text and shall provide a range of such sizes from 50% of the default character size to 200% of the default character size. **Fonts:** - a. Captioning shall be implemented such that fonts are available to implement the eight fonts required by CEA-708 and listed below. Users must be provided with the ability to assign the fonts included on their apparatus as the default font for each of the eight styles. - b. Decoders must support the eight fonts listed below. Caption providers may specify 1 of these 8 font styles to be used to write caption text. The styles specified in the “font style” parameter of the SetPenAttributes command are numbered from 0 through 7. - c. The following is a list of the 8 required font styles. For information purposes only, each font style references one or more popular fonts which embody the characteristics of the style: - (i) 0—Default (undefined) - (ii) 1—Monospaced with serifs (similar to Courier) - (iii) 2—Proportionally spaced with serifs (similar to Times New Roman) - (iv) 3—Monospaced without serifs (similar to Helvetica Monospaced) - (v) 4—Proportionally spaced without serifs (similar to Arial and Swiss) - (vi) 5—Casual font type (similar to Dom and Impress) - (vii) 6—Cursive font type (similar to Coronet and Marigold) - (viii) 7—Small capitals (similar to Engravers Gothic)

- d. Font styles may be implemented in any typeface which the decoder manufacturer deems to be a readable rendition of the font style, and need not be in the exact typefaces given in the example above. Decoders must include the ability for users to choose among the eight fonts. The decoder must display the font chosen by the caption provider unless the user chooses a different font. **Caption background color and opacity:** Captioning shall be implemented such that the caption background may be displayed in the 64 colors defined in CEA-708 and such that users are provided with the ability to override the authored color for the caption background and select from a palette of at least 8 colors including: white, black, red, green, blue, yellow, magenta, and cyan. Captioning shall be implemented such that users are provided with the ability to vary the opacity of the caption background and select between opaque, semi-transparent, and transparent background opacities. **Character edge attributes:** Captioning shall be implemented such that character edge attributes may be displayed and users are provided the ability to select character edge attributes including: no edge attribute, raised edges, depressed edges, uniform edges, and drop shadowed edges. **Caption window color:** Captioning shall be implemented such that the caption window color may be displayed in the 64 colors defined in CEA-708 and such that users are provided with the ability to override the authored color for the caption window and select from a palette of at least 8 colors including: white, black, red, green, blue, yellow, magenta, and cyan. Captioning shall be implemented such that users are provided with the ability to vary the opacity of the caption window and select between opaque, semi-transparent, and transparent background opacities. **Language:** All players and devices must implement the ability to select between caption tracks in additional languages when such tracks are present and provide the ability for the user to select simplified or reduced captions when such captions are available and identify such a caption track as “easy reader.” **Preview and setting retention:**

- a. All players and devices must provide the ability for the user to preview default and user selection of the caption features required by this section, and must retain such settings as the default caption configuration until changed by the user. - b. **As of August 17, 2026:** Video players must also provide the ability for the user to preview the appearance of closed captions while changing the caption features required by this section. The preview must be overlaid on the programming the user is currently watching. The user must be able to change the caption features and preview their appearance without exiting the video player. (Note: Stock text may be used for the caption preview.) - c. Players may leverage device-level caption settings but must also meet the preview requirements in (a) and (b) above.

**Discoverability of caption controls.(as of August 17, 2026):** - a. All user controls for adjusting caption display characteristics must be provided in one area of the settings that is accessed by an easy-to-locate and simple-to-use mechanism such as a button, key, or icon. - b. Usability testing must be conducted with consumers and disability groups to determine if the controls can be easily found, and efforts must be made to correct problems identified during that testing. (Note: Making the controls available solely or primarily through voice control does not meet this requirement.)
_Applicability:
This requirement applies to - Devices capable of displaying video programming, such as laptops, smartphones, and gaming consoles, and - First-party video players that Microsoft preinstalls on a device or requires end-users to install on a device.

The FCC defines “video programming” as “programming provided by, or generally considered comparable to programming provided by, a television broadcast station, but not including consumer-generated media.” This requirement does not apply to - Applications with built-in players that are only used for video creation or editing. - Video communications (See the MAS 6.6 series for applicable requirements.)

- Publish a link to the accessibility conformance report. 
	- Websites: A link to the [France Accessibility Statements](https://www.microsoft.com/fr-fr/accessibility/accessibilite/declarations) page must be included on the site’s home page, unless the site uses the Universal Header Footer.
	- Mobile Applications: A link to the [France Accessibility Statements](https://www.microsoft.com/fr-fr/accessibility/accessibilite/declarations) page must be included
		- on the application’s related website, unless the website uses the Universal Header Footer, or 
		- at the point of download (for example, in the app store listing).
	- Online software and hardware: A link to the [France Accessibility Statements](https://www.microsoft.com/fr-fr/accessibility/accessibilite/declarations) page must be published on the software or hardware’s related website, unless the website uses the Universal Header Footer.
- Accessibility testing must include the following components, if applicable:
     - Homepage
     - Contact page
     - Legal notice page
     - Accessibility page  
     - Site map page
     - Help page 
     - Login page
     - At least one page from each type of online service, including any search functionality available on such page
     - At least one downloadable document for each type of online service
     - All process-related pages (for example, data entry forms, online transactions/purchases, registration)

_Title: Additional Documentation for EAA Devices and Operating Systems
_Requirement:
Devices and operating systems must include accessible instructions that are available (a) on the product itself, (b) through the use of the product, or (c) on a website. The instructions must be available when the device or operating system is placed on the market. The instructions must describe: • the product’s accessibility features and how to operate them • the product’s interoperability with assistive technologies, including a list of the assistive technologies tested with the product • the product’s user interface, including features and functionality addressing the following requirements: - if the product provides communication, including interpersonal communication, operation, information, control and orientation, providing it via more than one sensory channel; including providing alternatives to vision, auditory, speech and tactile elements - if the product uses color to convey information, indicate an action, require a response or identify elements, providing an alternative to color - if the product uses audible signals to convey information, indicate an action, require a response or identify elements, providing an alternative to audible signals - if the product uses visual elements, providing flexible ways of improving vision clarity - if the product uses audio, providing user control of volume and speed, and enhanced audio features including the reduction of interfering audio signals from surrounding products and audio clarity - if the product requires manual operation and control, providing for sequential control and alternatives to fine motor control, avoiding the need for simultaneous controls for manipulation, and using tactile discernible parts - avoiding modes of operation requiring extensive reach and great strength - avoiding triggering photosensitive seizures - protecting the user’s privacy when they use accessibility features - providing an alternative to biometrics identification and control - ensuring consistency of functionality and providing enough, and flexible amounts of, time for interaction - providing software and hardware for interfacing with assistive technologies - additional information for self-service terminals: - providing for text-to-speech technology - allowing for the use of personal headsets - where a timed response is required, alerting the user via more than one sensory channel - giving the user an opportunity to extend the time given - using an adequate contrast and tactilely discernible keys and controls, when keys and controls are available - not requiring an accessibility feature to be activated in order to enable a user who needs the feature to turn it on - when the product uses audio or audible signals, compatibility with assistive devices and technologies, including hearing technologies such as hearing aids, telecoils, cochlear implants and assistive listening devices - additional information for e-readers: - providing text-to-speech technology - additional information for electronic communications devices: - when such products have text capability in addition to voice, providing for the handling of real time text and supporting high fidelity audio - when such products have video capabilities in addition to or in combination with text and voice, providing for the handling of total conversation including synchronized voice, real time text, and video with a resolution enabling sign language communication - ensuring effective wireless coupling to hearing technologies - avoiding interference with assistive devices - additional information for devices used to access audiovisual media services: - making available the accessibility components provided by the audiovisual media service provider, for user access, selection, control, and personalization and for transmission to assistive devices
See the Guideline tab for link to documentation template.
_Applicability:
This requirement applies to devices and operating systems subject to the EAA:
•	general purpose consumer computer hardware systems and their operating systems.
•	Consumer equipment whose main purpose is electronic communications
•	Consumer equipment whose main purpose is accessing audiovisual media services
•	E-readers
•	ATMs, travel kiosks, and other self-service terminals
_Guidance: MAS 10.01.01: Additional Documentation for EAA Devices and Operating Systems is based on this European Union law: - European Accessibility act Annex I section I

Special rules for specific services: - Where a first-party device is designed specifically to provide the service (for example, a mobile phone configured to access a particular mobile operator’s network), a description of how to use the service with the device must be provided, as well as information about the devices’ accessibility characteristics and interoperability with assistive technology. - E-commerce services must publish information about the accessibility of the products and services they sell, if that information is provided by the responsible product manufacturer, importer, or distributor or service provider.

_Title: CE Marking and Documentation for EAA Devices and Operating Systems
_Requirement:
Prior to being placed on the European Union market, conformance to the EAA must be certified by:

•	Including the European Accessibility Act in the EU Declaration of Conformity (DOC).
     - The DOC must include the regulatory model number.
     - Notes:
          - To be EAA-conformant, devices (hardware, packaging, and user interface) and operating systems must support all             applicable MAS. 
          - Publishing the DOC can be a lengthy process, so this process should be started six months before placing a                 product on the EU market, when possible.
•	Affixing the CE Mark to a device or including an image of the CE Mark in an easily discoverable location in an operating system.
•	Preparing Technical Documentation by creating an entry in the Accessibility Assessment Tool (AAT) and completing all applicable sections, including Section 13. EAA Technical Documentation.
     -  the Technical Documentation must be published internally and sent to the internal Microsoft team responsible              for the CE Mark [MS Regulatory Compliance](mailto:regcomp@microsoft.onmicrosoft.com)
_Applicability:
This requirement applies to all devices and operating systems subject to the EAA:
•	general purpose consumer computer hardware systems and their operating systems.
•	Consumer equipment whose main purpose is electronic communications
•	Consumer equipment whose main purpose is accessing audiovisual media services
•	E-readers
•	ATMs, travel kiosks, and other self-service terminals
_Guidance: MAS 10.01.02: CE Marking and Documentation for EAA Devices and Operating Systems is based on these European Union laws and guidance documents: - European Accessibility Act - Blue Guide **EAA Article 7:** Obligations of manufacturers 1. When placing their products on the market, manufacturers shall ensure that the products have been designed and manufactured in accordance with the applicable accessibility requirements of this Directive. 2. Manufacturers shall draw up the technical documentation in accordance with Annex IV and carry out the conformity assessment procedure set out in that Annex or have it carried out. Where compliance of a product with the applicable accessibility requirements has been demonstrated by that procedure, manufacturers shall draw up an EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.
